deviation: The draft cuts availability to 97.0% (below the 99.5% fallback) and makes it only a "commercially reasonable efforts" obligation. It adds broad exclusions, removes service credits, and says a miss is not a breach, so Arcadia's only remedy is good-faith discussion, which is exclusive. Separately, 5.2 allows 168 hours (7 days) to notify security incidents affecting Customer Data, which is far too long and risks breaching Arcadia's data protection and regulatory notice duties.
suggested_text: 5.1 The Supplier shall ensure the Services are available at least 99.9% of the time in each calendar month, excluding only scheduled maintenance notified to the Customer at least five (5) business days in advance and agreed maintenance windows. 5.2 The Supplier shall notify the Customer of any actual or reasonably suspected security incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and in any event within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of it, and shall provide information and cooperation reasonably requested by the Customer. 5.3 If availability in any month falls below 99.9%, the Supplier shall issue service credits of 5% of the monthly fees for each full 1% shortfall. Service credits are without prejudice to the Customer's other rights and remedies, and repeated or material failure to meet the service level shall constitute a material breach of this Agreement entitling the Customer to terminate.
